# zlat2c

> Converts a double-complex triangular matrix to a single-complex triangular matrix with overflow checking.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zlat2c from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zlat2c';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zlat2c( order, uplo, N, A, LDA, SA, LDSA ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout (`'row-major'` or `'column-major'`) |
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | Specifies whether `A` is upper or lower triangular |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix `A` |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | Input matrix |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `A` |
| `SA` | `Complex64Array`<br><sub>M × N</sub> | **out** · Output matrix |
| ↳ `LDSA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of `SA` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: A is upper triangular;
  -   `= 'L'`: A is lower triangular.
- `N`: The number of rows and columns of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the N-by-N triangular coefficient matrix A.
- `SA`: Only the `UPLO` part of `SA` is referenced. On exit, if `INFO=0`, the N-by-N coefficient matrix `SA`; if $\mathrm{INFO}>0$, the content of the `UPLO` part of `SA` is unspecified.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (`0` = success, `1` = entry outside single-precision range)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be a valid matrix triangle
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` fifth argument must be greater than or equal to `max(1,N)`

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zlat2c.strided(
    uplo,
    N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    SA, strideSA1, strideSA2, offsetSA
) → integer
```

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `uplo` | `MatrixTriangle` | Specifies whether `A` is upper or lower triangular |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix `A` |
| `A` | `Complex128Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | Input matrix |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `A` |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `A` |
| `SA` | `Complex64Array`<br><sub>M × N</sub> | **out** · Output matrix |
| ↳ `strideSA1` | `integer` | Stride of the first dimension of `SA` |
| ↳ `strideSA2` | `integer` | Stride of the second dimension of `SA` |
| ↳ `offsetSA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `SA` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `uplo`:

  -   `= 'U'`: A is upper triangular;
  -   `= 'L'`: A is lower triangular.
- `N`: The number of rows and columns of the matrix A. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the N-by-N triangular coefficient matrix A.
- `SA`: Only the `UPLO` part of `SA` is referenced. On exit, if `INFO=0`, the N-by-N coefficient matrix `SA`; if $\mathrm{INFO}>0$, the content of the `UPLO` part of `SA` is unspecified.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: status code (`0` = success, `1` = entry outside single-precision range)

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid matrix triangle

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit.
-   `= 1`: an entry of the matrix A is greater than the SINGLE PRECISION overflow threshold, in this case, the content of the `UPLO` part of `SA` in exit is unspecified.

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `zlat2c()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`ZLAT2C`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/zlat2c.f).
-   The single-precision overflow threshold is IEEE 754 binary32's `RMAX` (approximately `3.4028e+38`). If any referenced entry of `A` has a real or imaginary part outside `[-RMAX, RMAX]`, the routine returns `1` and leaves the referenced triangle of `SA` in an unspecified state.
-   Each real and imaginary component is rounded independently via `Math.fround`.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import Complex64Array from '@stdlib/array/complex64/lib/index.js';
import zlat2c from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/zlat2c';

const N = 3;
const A = new Complex128Array( N * N );
const SA = new Complex64Array( N * N );
let i;

for ( i = 0; i < N * N; i++ ) {
	A.set( [ i + 1, ( i + 1 ) * 0.5 ], i );
}

const info = zlat2c( 'column-major', 'upper', N, A, N, SA, N );
console.log( 'info = %d', info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `ZLAT2C`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZLAT2C converts a COMPLEX\*16 triangular matrix, `SA`, to a COMPLEX triangular matrix, A.

RMAX is the overflow for the SINGLE PRECISION arithmetic ZLAT2C checks that all the entries of A are between -RMAX and RMAX. If not the conversion is aborted and a flag is raised.

This is an auxiliary routine so there is no argument checking.

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
